Note that 5 never divides ite because 5 is prime. Thus, we can pair up the terms: since ite \(\equiv-(5-i) t e \bmod 5\),

\[\left\lfloor\frac{i t e}{5}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{(5-i) t e}{5}\right\rfloor=\frac{i t e}{5}+\frac{(5-i) t e}{5}-1\]

Thus

\[\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i=1}^{4} \sum_{t=1}^{4} \sum_{e=1}^{4}\left\lfloor\frac{\text { ite }}{5}\right\rfloor & =\left(\sum_{i=1}^{4} \sum_{t=1}^{4} \sum_{e=1}^{4} \frac{i t e}{5}\right)-\frac{4^{3}}{2} \\
& =\frac{1}{5}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{4} i\right)^{3}-\frac{64}{2} \\
& =\frac{1}{5}(10)^{3}-32 \\
& =2 \cdot 100-32 \\
& =168
\end{aligned}\]
